key: #   why      one sentence. Editorial.
thermopylae
name: Thermopylae
why: A strip between cliff and sea — in 480 BC the only road south into Greece for an army, and the coast has silted several kilometres since.

key: hellespont
name: The Hellespont
why: The narrowest crossing between Europe and Asia Minor; an army moving between the two continents on foot comes here or goes around the Black Sea.

key: bosphorus
name: The Bosphorus
why: The other crossing, and the reason a city was founded on it.

key: gibraltar
name: The Strait of Gibraltar
why: Fourteen kilometres between two continents and the only sea door to the Mediterranean.

key: bab-el-mandeb
name: Bab-el-Mandeb
why: The southern gate of the Red Sea; everything between the Mediterranean and the Indian Ocean passes it.

key: hormuz
name: The Strait of Hormuz
why: The mouth of the Persian Gulf.

key: malacca
name: The Strait of Malacca
why: The sea road between the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea.

key: oresund
name: The Oresund
why: The Baltic's door, and why a toll castle stands at Helsingor.

key: khyber
name: The Khyber Pass
why: The road from Central Asia into the Indian subcontinent; invaders of India come through here or by sea.

key: brenner
name: The Brenner Pass
why: The lowest crossing of the main Alpine chain, and the reason Italy and Germany have always been able to reach each other.

key: great-st-bernard
name: The Great St Bernard Pass
why: An Alpine crossing usable by an army, which most are not.

key: roncevaux
name: Roncevaux Pass
why: A way through the western Pyrenees, and a defile where a rearguard can be destroyed.

key: cilician-gates
name: The Cilician Gates
why: A cleft through the Taurus and the road from Anatolia into Syria.

key: shipka
name: The Shipka Pass
why: The crossing of the Balkan range between the Danube plain and Thrace.

key: iron-gates
name: The Iron Gates
why: Where the Danube cuts through the Carpathians — a gorge that is both a road and a wall.

key: moravian-gate
name: The Moravian Gate
why: The low ground between the Sudetes and the Carpathians; the way between the North European Plain and the Danube.

key: smolensk-gate
name: The Smolensk Gate
why: Dry ground between the Dvina and the Dnieper, with marsh either side — the land road to Moscow.

key: corinth
name: The Isthmus of Corinth
why: Six kilometres joining the Peloponnese to the mainland; a wall here closes off a peninsula.

key: suez
name: The Isthmus of Suez
why: The land bridge between Africa and Asia.

key: panama
name: The Isthmus of Panama
why: The narrow join between two continents and two oceans.

key: tempe
name: The Vale of Tempe
why: The gorge between Olympus and Ossa; the northern door into Thessaly, and why Thermopylae mattered once it was abandoned.

key: caudine-forks
name: The Caudine Forks
why: A defile a Roman army walked into and could not walk out of.

key: megiddo
name: The Pass of Megiddo
why: Where the coast road crosses the Carmel ridge; armies between Egypt and Mesopotamia have fought here for three thousand years.

key: pripet
name: The Pripet Marshes
why: Impassable wetland the size of a country — it split the Eastern Front in two in both world wars, and neither side could close the gap.

key: fens
name: The Fens
why: Waterlogged ground that held out against the Normans; drained in the seventeenth century and now farmland.

key: pontine
name: The Pontine Marshes
why: Malarial marsh on Rome's own doorstep, drained under Mussolini.

key: dutch-water-line
name: The Dutch Water Line
why: A country flooding its own fields on purpose — a wall made of shallow water, too deep to walk and too shallow to sail.

key: teutoburg
name: The Teutoburg Forest
why: Forest and bog together; three legions went in and Roman expansion into Germany ended.

key: sudd
name: The Sudd
why: A papyrus swamp that closed the upper Nile to travel and kept its source unknown to the Mediterranean world.

key: rub-al-khali
name: The Rub al Khali
why: The Empty Quarter — sand on a scale that is not crossed but gone around.

key: taklamakan
name: The Taklamakan
why: The desert the Silk Road splits to avoid, north and south, and rejoins beyond.

key: danube-delta
name: The Danube Delta
why: Reed and channel where the river meets the sea; a barrier at the end of a road.

key: everglades
name: The Everglades
why: Sawgrass and shallow water, and the reason a war against the Seminole could not be won.
